text:
maya: Heads-up — perm graph renderer is showing route quotas attached to the parent role instead of the scoped route. Screenshot in thread :eyes:

sam: I noticed weird counts in the console yesterday during the canary, thought it was telemetry noise. repro steps?

maya: quick repro: open Role > 'Platform Engineer' > toggle 'visualize graph'. The quota badge (e.g. 100r/m) shows on the role node, but if you expand the route nodes the specific route has no quota.

ash_k: repro'd locally. Looks like the renderer flattens scope metadata when building the graph model. Minimal curl to fetch the shape:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -X GET "https://console.internal/api/v1/roles/role_123/graph?expand=routes,quotas"
```response snippet:```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id":"role_123","meta":{"quotas":[{"limit":100,"scope":"route:payments"}]}} ,
    {"id":"route_payments","meta":{}}
  ]
}
```so the backend serializes the quota on the role node and renderer assumes it's global.

irene: tagging product/ops: @irene — do we consider quotas on roles a valid model? We intended quotas to be route-bound in most tenant setups.

maya: product intent is quotas attach to route-scopes, but we allowed role-level overrides in the API (rare). The renderer should visualize scope ownership, not naive attachment.

ben_prod: I can see two fixes: backend emits explicit ownership (owner: route_id) OR renderer resolves by looking up scope keys. Backend change is safer for long-term but touches many rollouts.

ash_k: backend emits owner would be clean. Quick patch: add owner field in the graph API and keep current shape backward-compatible. Then renderer checks owner -> fallbacks to existing behavior.

sam: telemetry side: our dashboard counts (per-route quota badges) are derived from renderer outputs for screenshots and marketing snapshots. If we change shape, dashboards might drop counts. We need migration + a flag to keep old counts for 2 weeks.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: canary/console-visualizer v2 started at 1735009920 by ci-pipeline

maya: plan proposal — short-lived feature flag `perm_graph_owner` gated to 10% tenants, backend emits `owner` field, renderer reads owner if present. Add a telemetry counter `perm_graph.owner_mapped` and `perm_graph.owner_fallback`.

irene: agree. Ops: add an alert if fallback rate > 5% after rollout window. Also include a migration job to backfill owner for existing role-level quotas.

ben_prod: I'll own the backfill job. Will run as dry-run for 24h then merge.

ash_k: I'll open two PRs: backend (owner field + tests) and renderer (owner-aware placement). Keep the old rendering logic under flag.

sam: add to release checklist: update dashboard ETL mapping, bump snapshot job to use new field when flag enabled. I'll handle ETL change and coordinate with marketing snapshots.

maya: thanks. Can we get a quick UX oob check? small change in graph layout might shift nodes and cause overlap.

ash_k: will add node spacing guard and test with the largest tenant graph (prod-sim).

deploy-bot: Canary finished: 1735009960 — rollout at 10% started.

maya: cool — follow-up in #incidents if anything spikes. If fallback alerting fires, pause rollout and revert the flag. :thumbsup:

sam: noted. I'll ship the dashboard fallback mapping later today.

irene: thanks everyone. small doc update for console release notes would be good (what changed and how to interpret quota badges).

maya: done — I'll add a short blurb and link to the backfill run when complete.
